# orgx

> Org-mode and Markdown CLI for humans and AI agents, and a
> Logseq-shaped vault (journals, pages, graph) built on plain org
> files. Agents live in the graph: they journal with attribution,
> link nodes by ID, and everything they write is text the human
> reads in Emacs.

Key facts:

- Vault: a directory marked by `.orgx/`, discovered by walking up
  like git. Layout: `journals/`, `pages/`, `whiteboards/`,
  `assets/`, `pages/contents.org`, `pages/flashcards.org` (read
  that page first). `orgx init` scaffolds it; an existing org-roam
  directory already works unmodified.
- Token-efficient document ops: `peek` (structure only), `get` (one
  section by ref), `find` (refs, not content), `set` (surgical
  edit). Stable refs are `path::ID:<uuid>`.
- GTD: `capture`, `promote`, `log`; LOGBOOK state logging; org
  timestamps with relative dates (`+1d`, `today`).
- Vault ops: `node new/list`, `daily [text] --as <author>`,
  `graph` (derived nodes/edges/broken links), `links`/`backlinks`.
- Contract: every command takes `--json`; outputs are versioned
  envelopes (`kind: orgx.<command>.v1`); errors are `orgx.error.v1`
  on stderr with a runnable `fix`. Reads never write; writes need
  `--yes` off-TTY.
- `orgx skills install` writes the embedded SKILL.md where agent
  runtimes look; a sync-guard test keeps skill and surface honest.

Docs:

- [README](README.md): install, quick start, agent contract
- [SKILL.md](skills/orgx/SKILL.md): the agent operating manual
- [ARCHITECTURE](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the four-layer frame and
  the vault design (why graph is derived, why no database)
- [schema](docs/schema.md): JSON kind registry and additive policy
